title: Fix the two-call wall-clock race in epic_25_schema_core_test.dart's SystemLocalDayClock.today() test
why: clock.today() and DateTime.now() are two independent wall-clock reads compared for equal year/month/day; if local midnight falls between the two calls the assertions intermittently disagree — a hairline but real flake source, exactly the class TQ-6 exists to keep out of test/ (test/ is not yet covered by the DateTime.now() audit grep that already protects lib/).
recommendation: Capture one DateTime.now() first and derive both the expected y/m/d and the clock.today() call from it, or bracket clock.today() between a before/after DateTime.now() pair instead of comparing to a second independent read.
acceptance_criteria: test reads the wall clock once (or brackets before/after) instead of comparing two independent DateTime.now()-derived values
